info.title: Genshin Impact API
info.description:
The Genshin Impact API, as it is actually registered.
Generated from the running route table by php/generate-api-spec.php and
angular/generate-openapi.mjs - not maintained by hand, and not annotated
onto the handlers. Regenerate with `npm run api` in angular/.
9 registered routes are left out: they reference tables and model classes that do not exist, and answer 500.

AdminUser.title: AdminUser
AdminUser.description: What /api/users answers with. Every read here is `SELECT USER_COLUMNS`, which is the users table minus the three columns that must never be published: the password hash, and the reset token with its expiry.

deleted.description: Disabling an account sets this; nothing is destroyed.

ApiError.title: ApiError
ApiError.description: What a failed request carries, whatever the status.

code.description: A stable name for the refusal, on the few that the caller has to tell apart rather than merely show. `error` is prose meant for a person and may be reworded at any time, so a page that has to *do* something different - offer to resend a confirmation rather than say the password was wrong - reads this instead. Absent on every refusal where the message is the whole answer. email_not_confirmed  the credentials were right, the address is not confirmed, and the account cannot be used yet invalid_token        a link that has expired, been used, or never was

AssetTrashResult.title: AssetTrashResult
AssetTrashResult.description: Deleting moves the file to the trash under a stamped name; nothing is lost.

url.description: Same as `path`, relative to the site root.

AuditLogEntry.title: AuditLogEntry
AuditLogEntry.description: One logged change. Two things differ from the `audit_logs` row: the username is joined in, and `changes` is decoded - the column stores it as JSON text.

changes.description: Column to { old, new }. Absent on an insert, which logs the whole row.

AuditLogUser.title: AuditLogUser
AuditLogUser.description: An account, reduced to what the audit filter needs to name it.

AuthMailRequested.title: AuthMailRequested
AuthMailRequested.description: The answer from the two endpoints that take an address and may send to it. Always the same, and says nothing about what was found. Whether there is an account behind an address, whether it still needs confirming, whether it has a password to reset - none of that is anything an endpoint open to the whole internet should be willing to tell apart.

AuthPending.title: AuthPending
AuthPending.description: What registration hands back: no session, because there is not one yet. The account exists and cannot be used until the address on it is confirmed, so the only useful things to say are which address the message went to and whether it actually went. `sent` false is not an error - the account is made either way - but it lets the page offer to try again instead of telling somebody to go and look for a message that was never posted.

AuthProviders.title: AuthProviders
AuthProviders.description: Which ways in this deployment offers, asked before anybody has signed in. The client id is public by design - it travels in the page and identifies the site to Google - so there is nothing here that the rendered button would not give away anyway. Null, and `google_enabled` false, while no client id is configured, which is how the site ships.

AuthSession.title: AuthSession
AuthSession.description: What a successful register or login hands back.

token.description: The bearer token. Every later request carries it.

AuthUser.title: AuthUser
AuthUser.description: An account as the auth endpoints describe it. Never carries the password.

has_password.description: Whether there is a password on the account at all.

password_login_enabled.description: Whether it is still accepted. Distinct from having one: an account can keep its password and ask for it not to be a way in.

google_email.description: The Google address that is connected, for the account page to show.

totp_enabled.description: Whether a code from an authenticator app is required to sign in.

recovery_codes_remaining.description: Unused recovery codes left. Zero when two-factor is off.

BackupTableCount.title: BackupTableCount
BackupTableCount.description: What /api/backups answers with. None of this is in a database. A backup is a set of dump files with a manifest beside them, so the manifest is the only place these shapes exist.

quiz.description: The quiz's name, which is what the URL uses.

state.description: The front end's own shape, stored as it arrives and handed back untouched. Nothing on this side reads into it.

RestoreRequest.description: Replacing a database with what is in a backup. `confirm` must be the database's own alias and `password` the caller's own. Both are checked again on the server: the browser is not what decides whether this is allowed.

SessionEntry.description: One session: where the account was signed in, how, and whether it still is. `ip` and `user_agent` are what the request carried, unexamined. They are shown so a person can recognise their own devices, not relied on for anything - a user agent is a string the caller chooses.

revoked_reason.description: Why it ended, where anything but its own expiry ended it.

active.description: Neither revoked nor expired - worked out here, against our own clock.

current.description: The session asking. The page will not offer to end this one by surprise.

SessionList.title: SessionList
SessionList.description: Every session this account has had, and how many attempts have failed since it last succeeded. The count is deliberately "since the last good sign-in" rather than a lifetime total: a number that only grows says nothing, and the question worth answering is whether somebody has been trying lately.

SessionsEnded.title: SessionsEnded
SessionsEnded.description: How many sessions "sign out everywhere else" actually ended.

SetOwnPasswordRequest.title: SetOwnPasswordRequest
SetOwnPasswordRequest.description: A first password, for an account that has none. No current password, because there is not one - being signed in is the proof, and getting signed in already took Google or a code from the account's own mailbox. Changing an existing one is ChangePasswordRequest.

toString.description: Returns a string representation of a string.

charAt.description: Returns the character at the specified index.

charCodeAt.description: Returns the Unicode value of the character at the specified location.

concat.description: Returns a string that contains the concatenation of two or more strings.

indexOf.description: Returns the position of the first occurrence of a substring.

lastIndexOf.description: Returns the last occurrence of a substring in the string.

localeCompare.description: Determines whether two strings are equivalent in the current locale. Determines whether two strings are equivalent in the current or specified locale.

match.description: Matches a string with a regular expression, and returns an array containing the results of that search. Matches a string or an object that supports being matched against, and returns an array containing the results of that search, or null if no matches are found.

replace.description: Replaces text in a string, using a regular expression or search string. Passes a string and {@linkcode replaceValue} to the `[Symbol.replace]` method on {@linkcode searchValue}. This method is expected to implement its own replacement algorithm. Replaces text in a string, using an object that supports replacement within a string.

search.description: Finds the first substring match in a regular expression search.

slice.description: Returns a section of a string.

split.description: Split a string into substrings using the specified separator and return them as an array.

substring.description: Returns the substring at the specified location within a String object.

toLowerCase.description: Converts all the alphabetic characters in a string to lowercase.

toLocaleLowerCase.description: Converts all alphabetic characters to lowercase, taking into account the host environment's current locale.

toUpperCase.description: Converts all the alphabetic characters in a string to uppercase.

toLocaleUpperCase.description: Returns a string where all alphabetic characters have been converted to uppercase, taking into account the host environment's current locale.

trim.description: Removes the leading and trailing white space and line terminator characters from a string.

length.description: Returns the length of a String object.

substr.description: Gets a substring beginning at the specified location and having the specified length.

valueOf.description: Returns the primitive value of the specified object.

codePointAt.description: Returns a nonnegative integer Number less than 1114112 (0x110000) that is the code point value of the UTF-16 encoded code point starting at the string element at position pos in the String resulting from converting this object to a String. If there is no element at that position, the result is undefined. If a valid UTF-16 surrogate pair does not begin at pos, the result is the code unit at pos.

includes.description: Returns true if searchString appears as a substring of the result of converting this object to a String, at one or more positions that are greater than or equal to position; otherwise, returns false.

endsWith.description: Returns true if the sequence of elements of searchString converted to a String is the same as the corresponding elements of this object (converted to a String) starting at endPosition – length(this). Otherwise returns false.

normalize.description: Returns the String value result of normalizing the string into the normalization form named by form as specified in Unicode Standard Annex #15, Unicode Normalization Forms.

repeat.description: Returns a String value that is made from count copies appended together. If count is 0, the empty string is returned.

startsWith.description: Returns true if the sequence of elements of searchString converted to a String is the same as the corresponding elements of this object (converted to a String) starting at position. Otherwise returns false.

anchor.description: Returns an `<a>` HTML anchor element and sets the name attribute to the text value

fontcolor.description: Returns a `<font>` HTML element and sets the color attribute value

fontsize.description: Returns a `<font>` HTML element and sets the size attribute value

link.description: Returns an `<a>` HTML element and sets the href attribute value

padStart.description: Pads the current string with a given string (possibly repeated) so that the resulting string reaches a given length. The padding is applied from the start (left) of the current string.

padEnd.description: Pads the current string with a given string (possibly repeated) so that the resulting string reaches a given length. The padding is applied from the end (right) of the current string.

trimEnd.description: Removes the trailing white space and line terminator characters from a string.

trimStart.description: Removes the leading white space and line terminator characters from a string.

trimLeft.description: Removes the leading white space and line terminator characters from a string.

trimRight.description: Removes the trailing white space and line terminator characters from a string.

matchAll.description: Matches a string with a regular expression, and returns an iterable of matches containing the results of that search.

replaceAll.description: Replace all instances of a substring in a string, using a regular expression or search string.

at.description: Returns a new String consisting of the single UTF-16 code unit located at the specified index.

ThemeChanged.title: ThemeChanged
ThemeChanged.description: Echoed back so the caller can confirm what was stored.

TotpCodeRequest.title: TotpCodeRequest
TotpCodeRequest.description: A code from the authenticator app, or a recovery code where one is allowed. Turning two-factor off and asking for new recovery codes both require one, for the same reason changing a password requires the old one: somebody at a signed-in machine should not be able to quietly remove it.

TotpRecoveryCodes.title: TotpRecoveryCodes
TotpRecoveryCodes.description: The way back in when the phone is gone. Returned exactly once, when they are generated, because only their hashes are kept. There is no endpoint that can show them again - asking for another set replaces them.

TotpSetup.title: TotpSetup
TotpSetup.description: A freshly issued two-factor secret, on its way to an authenticator app. Both forms of the same thing: the URI is what a QR code encodes, and the secret is what somebody types when there is no camera to hand. Nothing is required of the account until a code computed from it has been handed back.

secret.description: Base32, as an authenticator expects it typed.

uri.description: The otpauth:// URI a QR code carries.

TranslationAdminView.title: TranslationAdminView
TranslationAdminView.description: Everything the translation editor draws in one request. Deliberately includes keys nothing has translated yet: those are the rows that need attention.

languages.description: The rows, so a disabled language still lists its own settings.

TranslationBundle.title: TranslationBundle
TranslationBundle.description: One language's strings, keyed by translation key. English is merged underneath every bundle by the server, so a key with no string in this language still answers with something readable.

TranslationBundleResponse.title: TranslationBundleResponse
TranslationBundleResponse.description: `GET /api/translations/{code}` - the strings, and which language they turned out to be. An unknown or retired code answers in the fallback rather than failing, so `language` is worth reading: it is not always the code that was asked for. `values` is a flat key-to-string map with English merged underneath, so a key with no string in this language still answers with something readable.

TranslationGridKey.title: TranslationGridKey
TranslationGridKey.description: One key in the editing grid, with what every language has for it.

site.description: `common` when every site loads it, otherwise the site that owns it.

create_missing_keys.description: Off by default: an import should not invent keys nobody declared.

TranslationKey.title: TranslationKey
TranslationKey.description: A row of `translation_keys` as the API reads it back.

UserStamp.description: A user as an audit column reports them. `created_by` and `updated_by` hold an id in the database, but DbQuery's includeExternal() swaps the id for the row before answering, so what arrives is the user, or null where the account has since gone.
